selection_rules: source.base is relative to the root; root "repo" is the experiment checkout (build --source-repo), the others are the cluster directories of roots, or their local copies (roots[root].local) for machine "local".

Globs (include, per_run_files) are matched by the builder's own walk of the tree, not pathlib: "*" and the other wildcards stay within one folder, "**" spans any number of folders. Only regular files are members; directories never are.
include: glob patterns relative to base (default "**/*" when there is no id_list or file_list). An include pattern that selects nothing, or a literal include that is missing, stops the build.

Symlinks are never released: a symlink (dangling or not) or symlinked folder that a selection reaches, and an unreadable folder, stop the build. The links the planners use are listed in path_remap.links.

id_list: gzip file under id_list_root (relative to this spec's folder), one run folder per line relative to base (a bare run id when base is the runs folder), sorted by code point, no duplicates, no run inside another listed run; runs = its line count. per_run_files are globs relative to each run folder; a pattern that selects nothing in any run stops the build, and so does a per_run_required file missing from any run. include may add files next to an id_list; a file included inside a listed run folder joins that run (same shard, counted in its episode row).
file_list: gzip file under id_list_root, one member file per line relative to base; every line must exist.
Id and file list lines must be normalised relative paths: no "..", ".", empty part, absolute path, trailing "/" or surrounding spaces.
exclude: fnmatch patterns ("*" also matches "/") tested against the member path relative to base.

restore_root: members restore to <restore_root>/<path relative to base>. No two items restore the same path unless they name each other in shared_paths_with and the files are byte-identical (no item does).

known_sha256: member path relative to base (or a file name unique in the item) -> sha256 known before the build (of record, cited in traversing/results/README.md or traversing/docs/evidence.md, or computed 09-29); the build stops on a mismatch.

known_params: checkpoint (.pt/.pth, path relative to base) -> parameter count as verify_release.py counts it: the elements of every tensor of the checkpoint's state dict (a pickled module: its state_dict(); a dict of tensors: itself; else the first of its keys state, model, model_state_dict, state_dict that holds one; else the dict of tensors with the most elements found inside it), except batch-norm running_mean, running_var and num_batches_tracked and the buffers named in param_buffers (last key component). params_unrecorded lists checkpoints whose training record states no count (the value was computed 09-29). The build stops if either names no released checkpoint.

requires: items the downloader adds to the selection because this item relies on files released only there. It links only dependencies of evaluation size; an item whose table columns also count drives of a raw collection names that collection in its description instead.
episode_defaults: episodes.csv.gz values used when outcome.json and case.json lack the field.
path_remap: how the paths inside released task files map to release restore paths, and the symlinks to recreate (see its own description).
inventory_items: the 09-29 inventory entries this release item covers (old item names included).

description: How to turn a path written inside a released task file (drive task lists, pick task lists, job lists) into the release restore path of the file it names.

1. Absolute paths are used as they are. A relative path that starts with artifacts/ or assets/ is relative to the repository root. Any other relative path is joined to the root of the first relative_roots entry whose task_files glob ('*' stays within one folder) matches the task file's restore path, and normalised ('..' collapsed). Files matching task_files_exclude (metadata next to the task lists) are not task files.
2. The longest matching key of prefixes is replaced by its value (keys ending in '/' match folders, others one file). A repository-relative path without a matching key stays as it is.

3. If the result is not a released file but matches a copies rule, the task names a byte-identical renamed copy of a released pick route; recreate it from the 'of' path (the made_by command wrote them).

4. links: symlinks that the planners, the dataset builders and results/README.md go through; symlinks are never released. Recreate each from the repo root with: mkdir -p "$(dirname PATH)" && ln -s TARGET PATH (TARGET is relative to the link's folder). In the tracker by-arm views <route> runs over the 423 route ids of tracker_drive_folders (its run folder names without the __<arm> suffix); the v1 policy view is not a table arm and its drives are not released.

Every reference was resolved this way on 09-29; what does not resolve (collection inputs, arms outside the compact tables, one machine-specific file) is listed with reasons in the staging note path_remap_check.md.
